{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Read the data
sales = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Confirm the revenue column is string and has commas
print("Sample revenue values before cleaning:", sales['revenue'].head(10).tolist())

# Check for commas (thousands separators)
has_commas = sales['revenue'].str.contains(',', regex=False)
print(f"Number of revenue entries with commas: {has_commas.sum()}")
print(f"Sample with commas: {sales.loc[has_commas, 'revenue'].head(5).tolist()}")

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
sales['revenue_clean'] = sales['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Check for QA orders (revenue = 999999.99)
qa_orders = sales[sales['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99]
print(f"Number of QA orders: {len(qa_orders)}")
print(f"QA order IDs: {qa_orders['order_id'].tolist()}")

# But we are not using revenue for this question — only age of converters
# So we just need to confirm that revenue doesn't affect age analysis
# However, we must still ensure that only valid data is used

# Now, filter for converted customers who are not missing age
converted = sales[(sales['converted'] == 1) & (sales['customer_age'] != -1)]

# Compute mean age
mean_age = converted['customer_age'].mean()
print(f"Mean age of converted customers (valid only): {mean_age:.2f}")

# Also check: are there any refunded orders among the converted?
print(f"Number of converted orders: {len(converted)}")
print(f"Number of converted and refunded: {(converted['status'] == 'refunded').sum()}")"}
